 Thanks to his iconic and enduring role in Mad Men , Jon Hamm is one of the most important TV actors not only of his generation, but also of all time. In recent years, Hamm has settled into some solid TV roles in shows like Your Friends & Neighbors , which was written and created for TV by Jonathan Tropper . If Tropper’s name sounds familiar, it’s because he also penned the script for Shawn Levy ’s new Star Wars movie, Starfighter , which is set to hit theaters in 2028. While he’s certainly best known for his aforementioned roles in TV shows like Mad Men , Hamm is also famous for starring in some legendary crime thrillers over the years, such as The Town . Ben Affleck directs and stars in the 2010 Oscar-nominated crime drama, alongside Bosch ’s Titus Welliver .

 Despite the many notable roles under his belt, though, Hamm is always on the hunt for his next big TV project. He’s found exactly that, too, thanks to his role as Fred Heckman in American Hostage , the gripping legal thriller streaming on MGM+. The streamer debuted the first two episodes of American Hostage back on September 20, and new episodes have followed every week on the platform. The Season 1 finale of American Hostage is right around the corner, looming on November 1, but the show is not giving up any ground on MGM+ streaming charts. It’s still the most-watched show on the platform and among the most-watched shows in the world. The show was written and created for TV by Shawn Ryan , who is also famous for his work on The Shield (starring Walton Goggins ) and The Night Agent (starring Gabriel Basso ).

 Which Criminal Mastermind Would Be Your Nemesis? 
 Lecter · Joker · Moriarty · Chigurh 
 Four of the finest criminal minds ever put on screen. One of them would look at you and see something worth their time. Eight questions decide which one comes for you, why they picked you, and what they would want when they arrived. 
 🍷 Lecter 
 🃏 Joker 
 ♟️ Moriarty 
 🪙 Chigurh 
 MEET YOUR NEMESIS → 
 QUESTION 1 / 8 TARGET 
 01 
 What would a criminal mastermind notice about you first? 
 Great villains choose their opponents carefully. Something about you got their attention. 
 A My manners, and everything I am careful not to say. 
 B That I still believe people are basically decent. 
 C That I am clever, and quietly enjoy proving it. 
 D That I handle things myself, and always have. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 2 / 8 CONTACT 
 02 
 How do they make first contact? 
 The introduction tells you everything about what is coming next. 
 A A polite letter. Beautiful handwriting. Quietly wrong. 
 B Something on fire, with a message left beside it. 
 C A puzzle, left where only I would look. 
 D No contact. Just the aftermath, and a coin. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 3 / 8 CODE 
 03 
 What do you actually believe about right and wrong? 
 Every nemesis is really an argument about the thing you believe most. 
 A There are lines. Mine are private and absolute. 
 B Rules are the only thing keeping us from being animals. 
 C Morality is a system, and systems can be solved. 
 D Things happen. Most of it was never up to me. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 4 / 8 PRESSURE 
 04 
 What finally gets under your skin? 
 Everybody has a pressure point. Finding yours is the whole plan. 
 A Being seen clearly by somebody I cannot read. 
 B Watching good people do something ugly. 
 C Losing to someone who was simply better prepared. 
 D Having no move left that changes anything. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 5 / 8 DEFENCE 
 05 
 They have made their move. How do you fight back? 
 This is the part of the film where the audience finds out who you are. 
 A Carefully, and never where they expect to be touched. 
 B Loudly. I would rather lose than play their game. 
 C With a better plan. I can out-think this. 
 D Directly, once, with whatever is closest to hand. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 6 / 8 WEAKNESS 
 06 
 What would they use against you? 
 A good villain never brings a weapon you have not already handed them. 
 A My privacy. I have kept far too much to myself. 
 B My conscience. I will not cross the line they want. 
 C My ego. I cannot resist a worthy opponent. 
 D My certainty that I can handle it alone. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 7 / 8 ENDGAME 
 07 
 What do they actually want from you? 
 The money is never the point. Something else always is. 
 A To understand me better than anyone ever has. 
 B To prove I am no better than they are. 
 C To finally be beaten by someone worth the trouble. 
 D Nothing at all. I stepped into the wrong path. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 8 / 8 RECKONING 
 08 
 How does it end between the two of you? 
 Eight questions in, this is the one that decides who comes for you. 
 A A conversation I will be replaying for years. 
 B A choice forced on me that has no clean answer. 
 C One final move, and the better mind wins. 
 D A coin in the air, and nothing I can say. 
 REVEAL MY NEMESIS → 
 The Case File Is Complete 
 Your Nemesis Is… 
 Four criminal masterminds. One of them was always going to be yours.
 Here is who comes for you, why they picked you out of everyone available, and what they want from
 the encounter.
 The Silence of the Lambs · Hannibal · 1991–2002 
 Hannibal Lecter 
 Your nemesis does not want to beat you. He wants to know you
 completely, and he is patient enough to wait for it. The frightening part is how good the
 conversation is.
 Lecter is the most dangerous kind of opponent: the one who finds you interesting. He
 never raises his voice, because he has never needed to.
 You keep a great deal to yourself and you are careful about what you show. That reserve
 is exactly the door he would knock on.
 The films understood something other thrillers missed. The horror is not the violence.
 It is being perfectly understood by the wrong person.
 He would be unfailingly polite about all of it. That is the worst part.
 Batman · The Dark Knight · 1989–2019 
 The Joker 
 Your nemesis is not after money, territory or revenge. He is
 after a demonstration, and you are the person he has chosen to prove his point on.
 The Joker only picks opponents who believe in something. Your decency is not a defence
 against him. It is the entire reason he showed up.
 He has no plan you can predict and nothing you can take away, which removes every tool
 you would normally reach for.
 His whole argument is that you are one bad day away from being him, and you would spend
 the rest of your life proving him wrong.
 He would call it a magic trick. You would call it the worst night of your life.
 Sherlock Holmes · The Final Problem · Since 1893 
 Moriarty 
 Your nemesis respects you, which sounds flattering until you work
 out what it means. He chose you because nobody else was worth his time.
 Moriarty is the original criminal mastermind, the template every later one borrows from:
 a mind the equal of the hero's, pointed the wrong way.
 You enjoy being the cleverest person in the room. He is counting on exactly that, and he
 has already built the room.
 This is the rare nemesis who would be genuinely disappointed if you lost badly. He needs
 the game to be worth playing.
 It ends the way these things always end. Two people, one problem, and only one way down.
 No Country for Old Men · 2007 
 Anton Chigurh 
 Your nemesis has no personal interest in you whatsoever, and that
 is precisely what makes him unsurvivable. You are not a rival. You are a stop on the way.
 Chigurh does not negotiate, gloat or explain. He arrives, he asks one question, and the
 answer was decided long before you opened your mouth.
 You trust yourself to handle things. He is the one problem in the world that has no
 interest in how capable you are.
 No Country for Old Men rewrote the screen villain by removing the thing audiences
 quietly rely on: the sense that talking might work.
 Call it. He will wait.

 What Is ‘American Hostage’ About?
 Additional cast members for MGM+’s American Hostage include Giovanni Ribisi as Tony Kiritsis, William Jackson Harper as Ben Hairston, Mireille Enos as Barbara Heckman, Mark McKinney as Police Chief Gallagher, Kat Cunning as Ibby Hall, and Kristoffer Polaha as Dick Hall. The official synopsis for American Hostage , which has registered solid scores of 88% from critics and 94% from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes through its first few episodes, reads as follows: “Fred Heckman, a beloved local radio reporter, is thrust into the middle of a life-or-death crisis when hostage-taker Tony Kiritsis demands to be interviewed on his popular radio news program.”
 Check out American Hostage on MGM+ and stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of Jon Hamm’s future projects.
